P1.evidence: No setter suffix in the title and no setter referenced, so the read-back is not applicable. The frame was three-part — 'I just want to basically understand, like, what's going on, what have you tried, and where you're trying to get to' — with no 'what's in the way' or 'what you need'. Agreement was taken ('Sounds good?' / 'Yeah, sounds good'). The open question was replaced by the kettlebell-familiarity question, which happened to open everything: it produced the herniated discs inside the first ninety seconds.

P2.evidence: The most complete baseline in the batch bar one. Work was covered properly, including the physical toll of dentistry and a two-hour daily commute. Injuries were interrogated well — 'This back injury, when did it happen?', 'what actually happened?', 'this tightness, when does it happen?' — producing the disc levels and the sciatica. Diet, sleep and energy were all asked directly and honestly answered. Height, weight and body fat came out through the goal conversation rather than being asked for, and age was never established. There was no open health-conditions question: the digestive illness, the depression and the medication all surfaced incidentally, which is why P2c is partial rather than hit.

P3.evidence: A textbook ladder. 'Why do you want to get shredded?' produced the real answer, and the rep then did something better than the script asks — he separated the stated goal from the real one and said so: 'from what I'm hearing from you, it's actually, it's not about getting shredded anymore', which the prospect accepted with 'No. Correct.' The hobbies question landed soccer and cycling; the future-self question landed the dental practice and then the identity line, 'when I don't have a fit body or a fit mind, then I'm just like, who am I?' The single gap is P3f — 'who else does that impact' was never asked, and no partner, family or dependants were mentioned at any point in seventy-four minutes.

P4.evidence: Prior attempts covered (a trainer's PDF, an unstructured gym habit), what happened covered, and the why asked directly: 'why, until now, like, why are we still here? Like, why haven't you actually been able to make a change?' The prospect named the gap unaided — 'I don't have a plan anymore ... it's just nothing structured' and the mental health and gut issues behind it. P4f ran in substance through the ownership sequence: 'who's responsible, actually, for making this change?' followed by the challenge 'a lot of people are saying, oh, yeah, I'm going to get a coach and he's going to get me in the best shape, but they're not willing to put in the work.'

P5.evidence: P5a ran — 'if we're going to have the same conversation, like, one year down the line, and you won't actually make this change ... how would that affect you, like, your life?' — but the answer that came back was thin ('I wouldn't feel confident, feel healthy, feel myself') and the rep pivoted to the positive picture rather than staying in it. No 'why not?' The settle-for challenge appeared only later and as an assertion during the money conversation: 'if you're okay with staying where you are right now, physically, mentally, that's okay, but I know you're not.' Line in the sand was never asked; its place was taken by an unscripted and effective substitute, 'will you let me keep you accountable?'

P6.evidence: Both questions ran before any number. 'Is there anything outside of yourself that would stop you actually to committing to this fully?' — 'No.' — followed by 'Sure?' and a confirmation. Then after the pillars, 'if you had the right training, the right nutrition, and the real accountability from Trevor, which is built around your life, do you agree that you would actually get to, not super shredded, but healthy, confident' — '100%.' And a final commitment check before price: 'are you fully committed to showing up for yourself and doing the work to become the confident version 2.0 of Hiten?' — 'Yes.' A clear yes was in hand before anything was presented.

P11.evidence: No programme purchase, so none of the payment or onboarding steps were reachable. The $100 refundable deposit taken to hold a next-day call is not a P11 step.

objection_plays.detail: The front half ran cleanly and largely verbatim. The pre-emptive handling of 'do you have a payment plan?' used the coached line exactly — 'Most of the clients pay upfront. Why would you ask?' — which is the move the manager taught on 28 May. Isolation ran ('Firstly, finances aside ... there isn't anything else that's keeping you from being 100% sure'), the HOW reframe ran ('you're not in a... you're in a how-to-do-it place'), the move-mountains line ran, and permission was asked for. Then the financial picture stopped after one question: cash on hand ($15,000). Monthly surplus was never asked, number of credit cards was never asked, available credit per card was never asked, used versus available was never asked, and investments only came up because the prospect volunteered them. Without those numbers the rep was improvising against a prospect whose money is committed to a loan-qualification threshold.

Trigger explicit — 'can I think about it still ... I have to sleep on it'. Two moves ran: the why probe ('Sorry. Why not? Tell me, what's going through your head?') and the isolation reframe ('we're still talking about numbers, not is it that you actually want to do it'). The strongest available moves were left on the table, and they were unusually well set up: the rep had spent ten minutes on self-sabotage, the angel and the devil, and the version of Hiten who opens the practice, and never asked 'that man you want to be — how does HE decide right now?' or 'thinking isn't the problem. Deciding is.'

Trigger present through the August/September move and the practice-loan timeline. One OD move ran in substance — 'that's putting, again, more time into the future and not actually pulling the trigger and starting and betting on yourself' — and the rep inverted the delay argument well by tying inaction to the practice opening slipping. None of 'things never slow down', 'the longer you wait the harder this gets' or 'the only thing you can control is right now' were used.

The rep raised fear pre-emptively and skilfully — 'when the decision comes, the fear, for example, creeps in ... we humans, we are masters of self-sabotage' — and later converted it into a live diagnostic at the moment of price: 'Is there a devil on the shoulder right now? What's he saying?' That is a good improvisation and it produced the real objection. But none of the scripted resolution moves followed: no certainty question, no bridge, no plane, no burned-before. The fear was surfaced and then left standing.

Capital committed to a business-financing threshold, with no scripted play. The prospect is saving toward the $80,000-$100,000 a lender wants to see before approving a dental practice loan, and every dollar spent moves that date. This is not a can't-afford objection and not a won't-pay objection; it is a competing capital allocation with an external gatekeeper, and the open-wallet play has no move for it. The rep's counter — that poor health would delay the practice more — was the right instinct and had no script behind it.

notes: Process-wise this is close to the ceiling: full baseline, a complete goals ladder, a real root cause, and a clear commitment before the number, plus two genuinely skilled improvisations in reframing 'shredded' to function and in asking what the devil on the shoulder was saying. Two corrections. First, the financial picture stopped after one question, so the plan was built on a single number. Second, and independent of the outcome, the herniated discs surfaced at 00:01:28 and were never revisited as a condition of starting — that has to become a gate before this deal is worked further.
